roll_calls.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Housing for the 21st Century Act (H R 6644)
roll_calls.plain_language: This bill establishes and modifies various federal housing programs. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

roll_calls.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Concur in Senate Adt to House Adt to Senate Adt — Housing for the 21st Century Act (H R 6644)
roll_calls.plain_language: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act establishes and modifies various federal housing programs. This vote, under suspension of the rules, was on accepting the Senate's latest changes to the bill after the chambers traded versions, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea accepts the Senate's version; a Nay opposes it.

matches.bill_title: Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026

roll_calls.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7567)
roll_calls.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to modify the Renewable Fuel Standard's definition of "renewable biomass".” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

roll_calls.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7567)
roll_calls.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment adds hot rotisserie chicken as an eligible item to be purchased by SNAP benefits.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

roll_calls.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7567)
roll_calls.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “An amendment numbered 20 printed in Part B of House Report 119-628 to mandate a USDA report to Congress (after the SNAP restrictions pilots are completed) on implementation of the restrictions, outcomes, recommendations to Congress.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

roll_calls.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7567)
roll_calls.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to repeal and prohibit future implementation of the Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) rule mandating electronic identification (EID) eartags for bison and cattle moving interstate.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

roll_calls.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7567)
roll_calls.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment strikes several sections relating to pesticide labeling requirements.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

roll_calls.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7567)
roll_calls.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to preserve greyhound racing operations in West Virginia.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

roll_calls.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment, as Modified (H R 7567)
roll_calls.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment revises the Agriculture Advanced Research and Development Authority program to provide federal support for sustainable agriculture and innovative sustainability solutions.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

roll_calls.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7567)
roll_calls.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to add "soda" to the definition of ineligible items and defines soda as a carbonated beverage containing more than 1 gram of added sugar, artificial sweetener, or flavoring per serving.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

roll_calls.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7567)
roll_calls.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment removes certain emissions standards on farm equipment.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

roll_calls.question: On Motion to Recommit — Farm, Food, and National Security Act (H R 7567)
roll_calls.plain_language: H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) reauthorizes through FY2031 and modifies Department of Agriculture programs (the farm bill), including commodity support, conservation, nutrition assistance, farm credit, rural development, forestry, and crop insurance. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

roll_calls.question: On Passage — Farm, Food, and National Security Act (H R 7567)
roll_calls.plain_language: This bill reauthorizes through FY2031 and modifies Department of Agriculture programs (the farm bill), including commodity support, conservation, nutrition assistance, farm credit, rural development, forestry, and crop insurance. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

When families go to the grocery store, they feel the cost. The price of food is simply too high and our farmers are struggling under rising costs.

That is why I voted for H.R. 7567, the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026, which passed the House. Our farmers feed America, create jobs, and keep eastern North Carolina's agriculture-based economy strong. The Senate must act so we can get a Farm Bill to the President's desk. We have waited long enough.

conflicts.caption: These are overlaps in public records, not evidence of a deal. Lobbying can be for or against a bill, and donors' employers didn't necessarily give money.
conflicts.method: Each itemized donor dollar is counted once, under the industry of the donor's self-reported employer; an industry counts if at least one LD-2 client in it lobbied on any bill this member sponsored or voted on.
